claims.text: Toenail onychomycosis: itraconazole 200 mg once daily for 12 consecutive weeks.
claims.quote: The recommended dose is 200 mg (2 capsules) once daily for 12 consecutive weeks.
claims.locator: Dosage and Administration › Treatment of Onychomycosis › Toenails with or without fingernail involvement

claims.text: Fingernails only: 2 pulses of 200 mg twice daily for 1 week, separated by 3 weeks off.
claims.quote: The recommended dosing regimen is 2 treatment pulses, each consisting of 200 mg (2 capsules) b.i.d. (400 mg/day) for 1 week. The pulses are separated by a 3-week period without SPORANOX ® .
claims.locator: Dosage and Administration › Treatment of Onychomycosis › Fingernails only

claims.text: Take capsules with a full meal.
claims.quote: Capsules should be taken with a full meal to ensure maximal absorption.

claims.text: Boxed warning: not for onychomycosis with ventricular dysfunction such as CHF or a history of CHF; stop if heart failure signs or symptoms occur.
claims.quote: Capsules should not be administered for the treatment of onychomycosis in patients with evidence of ventricular dysfunction such as congestive heart failure (CHF) or a history of CHF. If signs or symptoms of congestive heart failure occur during administration of SPORANOX ® Capsules, discontinue administration.
claims.locator: Boxed Warning › Congestive Heart Failure and Cardiac Effects

claims.text: Boxed warning: many CYP3A4 substrates are contraindicated with itraconazole, eg methadone, disopyramide, dofetilide, dronedarone, quinidine and ergot alkaloids.
claims.quote: Coadministration of a number of CYP3A4 substrates are contraindicated with SPORANOX ® . Some examples of drugs that are contraindicated for coadministration with SPORANOX ® Capsules are: methadone, disopyramide, dofetilide, dronedarone, quinidine, isavuconazole, ergot alkaloids

claims.text: Rare serious hepatotoxicity, some within the first week: consider liver function monitoring in all patients; stop at once and test liver function if signs of liver dysfunction develop.
claims.quote: Rare cases of serious hepatotoxicity have been observed with SPORANOX ® treatment, including some cases within the first week. It is recommended that liver function monitoring be considered in all patients receiving SPORANOX ® . Treatment should be stopped immediately and liver function testing should be conducted in patients who develop signs and symptoms suggestive of liver dysfunction.
